title: Constant model of the generic stalk image
statement: Let $X$ be an irreducible scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], with generic point $\eta$ [def-sc-generic-point], and $\Lambda$ a commutative ring. Let $\varphi:F\to G$ be a monomorphism of $\Lambda$-module sheaves on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], with $G$ constant [def-constructible-constant]. There exist a $\Lambda$-module $N$ and a monomorphism $\alpha:N_X\to G$ from its constant sheaf, such that for every separably closed field $\Omega$ and geometric point $s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ above $\eta$, there is an isomorphism $e_s:(N_X)_s\simeq F_s$ satisfying $e_s\varphi_s=\alpha_s$. Stalks are those of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. No finiteness or extension over an open is asserted.

source.place: Tag 09BH, Proposition 59.74.1 (3), generic submodule and generator-lifting paragraphs

proof.text: Choose G isomorphic to the constant sheaf M. At the geometric point given by an algebraic closure of the residue field of eta, identify the stalk of constant M with M. Set N equal to the range submodule of the injective stalk map of phi. The range factorization is an isomorphism from N to that stalk of F.

The inclusion N into M induces alpha into G by the constant-sheaf functor. This functor preserves monomorphisms: constant presheaves preserve them componentwise and sheafification is left exact. Thus alpha is mono.

For another separably closed geometric point above eta, choose compatible separable closures of the residue field and compare stalks through them. Etale neighbourhoods and their pointed refinements yield the same stalk after separably closed extension. The comparison is natural in F and G and is the identity on the values of constant M. It therefore identifies exactly the same range N and supplies the required e_s compatible with alpha_s and phi_s. The zero range is included.
